title: Sample Quiz: Project Management Basics
subject: Project management
description: Nine questions across easy, medium and hard. A quick way to see how Quizbox works.

questions.prompt: The classic triple constraint of project management refers to:
questions.explanation: Scope, time (schedule) and cost are linked. A change to one usually affects the others.

questions.prompt: Which document formally authorises a project?
questions.explanation: The project charter formally authorises the project and gives the project manager authority to use resources.

questions.prompt: A risk is best described as:
options: A problem that has already happened
A change request that was rejected
An uncertain event that could affect project objectives
questions.explanation: A risk is uncertain and lies in the future. Once it actually happens, it becomes an issue.

questions.prompt: The critical path of a project is:
options: The path with the most expensive activities
The path with the most team members
The path with the most risks
The longest sequence of dependent activities, which sets the shortest possible project duration
questions.explanation: A delay to any critical path activity delays the project finish date unless the time is recovered.

questions.prompt: On a power/interest grid, a stakeholder with high power and low interest should generally be:
questions.explanation: High power and low interest means keep satisfied. High power and high interest means manage closely.

questions.prompt: A stakeholder asks for a new feature in the middle of the project. What should the project manager do first?
options: Add it straight away to keep the stakeholder happy
Refuse it because the scope is fixed
Ask the team to absorb it without telling anyone
Assess its impact on scope, time, cost and risk, then submit it through change control
questions.explanation: Changes should be evaluated and then formally approved or rejected, never quietly added.

questions.prompt: A project has a budget at completion (BAC) of $100,000, earned value (EV) of $40,000 and actual cost (AC) of $50,000. If current cost performance is expected to continue, what is the estimate at completion (EAC = BAC / CPI)?
Activity A (3 days) must finish before B (4 days) and C (6 days) can start. Activity D (2 days) starts when both B and C have finished. What is the total float of activity B?
questions.explanation: A-C-D takes 3 + 6 + 2 = 11 days and is the critical path. A-B-D takes 3 + 4 + 2 = 9 days. So B can slip by 11 - 9 = 2 days without delaying the project.

questions.prompt: A threat has a 30% probability and a $50,000 impact. An opportunity has a 20% probability and a $20,000 benefit. What is the net expected monetary value (EMV) of the two together?
